reviews.evidence: Both consumer Facts cite the actual bounded-operator exponential series. For A,T,D and A* the operators are finite matrices on R^n/C^n, hence bounded (e.g. norm <= Frobenius norm) on the finite-coordinate Banach space. Hurwitz consumer Proof 2.1–3.1 uses norm differentiability, similarity termwise and variation-of-constants; Lyapunov Proof 1.2 and 4.1 uses derivative Ae^(tA)=e^(tA)A and E(0)=I, also for A*. These are the exact supplier conclusions for bounded operators; no unbounded-generator or general Hille–Yosida premise is imported. No choice principle is required by this supplier.

reviews.evidence: Supplier claim 3 says compact subsets of a Hausdorff space are closed. The consumer compact tube C is in Euclidean R^(d+1), which is Hausdorff (disjoint metric balls separate unequal points), and Proof 2.1 explicitly constructs a convergent graph sequence with limit (b,xb). Closedness therefore puts this limit in C subset D. The ambient space need not be compact; supplier claim 4 is not used. The supplier finite-choice proof is ZF and requires no transferred arbitrary choice axiom.

reviews.evidence: All four direct suppliers are used in the actual continuous-residual proof, not merely as page context. Consumer Statement/Given/A1 explicitly assumes Countable Choice plus Dependent Choice and deps names both, meeting the sharp FTC assumptions. In Proof 2.1 q and error components are AC; Proof 3.1 Lambda is the indefinite integral of ell in L1, hence AC. The integral triangle bound gives |Lambda|<=M, the mean-value theorem bounds the derivative of exp(-x) on [-M,M], so Lipschitz composition applies on Lambda image; the product theorem then makes wq AC. Proof 4.1–5.1 applies sharp FTC to this AC real product on restricted compact intervals. All arguments use actual real representatives; no arbitrary AC-after-AC composition is inferred.

reviews.evidence: All six IDs are the correct formal integral suppliers, and actual uses retain integrability, measurability and restricted-interval hypotheses: Proof 3.1 bounds the indefinite integral of ell; Proof 4.1 proves w*rho in L1 by domination, applies linearity to h and h+, a.e. invariance on [a,t], and nonnegative monotonicity; Proof 5.1 splits the indefinite integral. Actual def-l-one-of-a-measure explicitly states that L1(mu) is the class of integrable representatives and defers a.e. equivalence classes to the later Banach-space page. This is a concrete incorrect supplier characterization, though the proof itself works with representatives and separately invokes a.e. invariance. Smallest correction: delete the clause ", with functions identified up to almost-everywhere equality" from consumer [L1]; preserve all statement hypotheses and the rich result. No correction was made in this read-only review.
